title: Non-Linear
body:
The single property that makes an [[Activation Function]] worth having. **Without it, depth is
worthless**, and this note owns the argument the rest of the folder cites.

## The collapse

Take two layers with no activation between them:

$$
\mathbf{a}^{(2)} = W^{(2)}\left(W^{(1)}\mathbf{x} + \mathbf{b}^{(1)}\right) + \mathbf{b}^{(2)}
= \underbrace{\left(W^{(2)}W^{(1)}\right)}_{W'}\mathbf{x} + \underbrace{\left(W^{(2)}\mathbf{b}^{(1)} + \mathbf{b}^{(2)}\right)}_{\mathbf{b}'}
$$

$W'$ is a single [[Matrix]] and $\mathbf{b}'$ a single [[Vector]], so the two layers **are** one
layer. Induct on that and a hundred layers are one layer. The reason is entirely
[[LINEAR ALGEBRA]]: a composition of [[Linear Transformation|linear transformations]] is a linear
transformation, and no arrangement of them escapes that.

So a deep network with no activation has exactly the expressive power of
[[Linear Regression]] and none of its advantages, since it has thrown away the closed-form
solution ([[Least Squares]]) in exchange for nothing. That is the whole argument. Insert any
non-linear $\sigma$ between the layers and the identity above stops holding, because $\sigma(Wx)$
cannot be rewritten as some $W'x$.

## What it buys

A linear model can only draw a hyperplane. `XOR` is the smallest thing that defeats one, which is
the [[Perceptron]]'s failure, and a single [[Hidden Layer]] of two units with any non-linearity
fixes it. Push that further and one sufficiently wide hidden layer can approximate any continuous
function to arbitrary accuracy. The non-linearity is what turns a family of hyperplanes into a
family that can bend.

Note how little is required: [[ReLU]] is $\max\{0,z\}$, two straight lines meeting at the origin,
and that single kink is enough. The function does not have to be smooth, exotic, or even
interesting. It has to not be a straight line.

## Related

- [[Activation Function]]: the general role, and the table of which one to use
- [[ReLU]], [[Sigmoid]], [[Leaky ReLU]]: the specific choices
- [[Hidden Layer]], [[Multilayer Perceptron]]: what depth means once this holds
- [[Linear Transformation]] and [[Matrix Multiplication]] ([[LINEAR ALGEBRA]], MATH 1203): the
  composition fact the collapse rests on
